items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Shorty Rodgers, like Shorty Rodgers on “Pam,” him and Ralph Burns put the ending on it.

ctx.x: Well you’ve had I think a quite remarkable career in that you’ve moved from one kind of music to another with great skill, and I guess you said it earlier in the interview that you helped people, you didn’t get in their way, you made them sound better.

I don’t know if I helped them, I didn’t get in their way, that was the big thing. You know like I guess they could play, but I didn’t think of it like that until now, when you get a little older you hear things, like you just was playing and I wasn’t up to them guys. Well to me, I didn’t have the knowledge — not Flip so much but Flip’s got knowledge about playing — but I mean some of the other guys like Ralph Burns for instance, I worked with Nelson Riddle, I didn’t realize that he was – Neal Hefti was another,…
